habit: Drink a full glass of water before your first tea or coffee.
Take a 5-minute walk after every meal; it helps blood sugar control.
Plan tomorrow's top three tasks before you shut the laptop.
Follow the 20-20-20 rule: every 20 minutes, look 20 feet away for 20 seconds.
Keep your phone out of the bedroom tonight.
Stand up for every phone call today.
Spend 10 minutes outdoors in morning daylight.
Write down three things you're grateful for.
Do one 'two-minute task' immediately instead of adding it to a list.
Eat one extra portion of vegetables today.
Turn off non-essential notifications for the whole day.
Take the stairs at least twice today.
Do a 5-minute breathing exercise: in for 4, hold for 4, out for 6.
Read 10 pages of a book instead of scrolling before bed.
Batch your email: check it three times today, not thirty.
Call a friend or relative you haven't spoken to in a month.
Pack a healthy snack (nuts, fruit, roasted chana) so you skip biscuits.
Block a 90-minute focus slot in your calendar with no meetings.
Tidy your desk for 5 minutes at the end of the day.
Replace one sugary drink with water, buttermilk or green tea.
Stretch your neck and shoulders for 2 minutes every two hours.
Spend 15 phone-free minutes fully playing with your child.
Say 'no' to one low-value meeting this week.
Learn one thing for 15 minutes: a course video, article or doc.
Have dinner at least 2–3 hours before bed.
Do a 'shutdown ritual': close tabs, note open loops, say 'done for today'.
Walk 8,000 steps today; break it into short walks.
Put your workout clothes out tonight for tomorrow morning.
Eat slowly: put the spoon down between bites at one meal.
Spend 5 minutes reviewing your week's spending.
workout: 7-minute circuit: 30 s each of jumping jacks, squats, push-ups, plank, lunges, crunches, rest 10 s between.
Brisk 30-minute walk, aiming to be slightly out of breath but able to talk.
Surya Namaskar: 6 rounds slowly, then 6 rounds at a steady pace.
Desk-friendly: 3 sets of 15 chair squats, 10 desk push-ups, 30 s wall sit.
Core: 3 rounds of 30 s plank, 15 bird-dogs per side, 15 glute bridges.
Stair climb: 10 minutes up and down, holding the rail if needed.
Mobility: 10 minutes of hip openers, cat-cow, thoracic rotations and hamstring stretches.
Skipping: 10 rounds of 1 minute on, 30 seconds rest.
Upper body: 3 sets of push-ups (knees if needed), 12 dips on a chair, 20 shoulder taps.
Legs: 3 sets of 15 squats, 12 reverse lunges per leg, 20 calf raises.
Yoga flow: Tadasana, Trikonasana, Bhujangasana, Balasana, 1 minute each, twice.
Interval walk: 3 minutes easy, 1 minute fast, repeated 6 times.
Cycling or swimming 30 minutes at an easy, conversational pace.
Balance: stand on one leg 30 s each side, 3 rounds; try with eyes closed.
Play with the kids: 20 minutes of tag, ball or dancing counts.
Rest day: gentle 20-minute walk and 10 minutes of stretching.
Pranayama: 5 minutes Anulom Vilom and 5 minutes Bhramari.
Full body: 3 rounds of 10 burpees, 15 squats, 10 push-ups, 30 s plank.
Posture set: 15 wall angels, 15 chin tucks, 15 band pull-aparts or arm circles.
Weekend: a 45-minute walk or light hike in Cubbon Park or Lalbagh.
sleep: Keep the same wake-up time every day, including weekends.
Dim screens and lights 60 minutes before bed.
Keep the bedroom cool, dark and quiet; an eye mask helps.
Avoid caffeine after 2 pm; it can stay in your system for 6+ hours.
If you can't sleep after 20 minutes, get up and read something dull in low light.
Keep naps under 30 minutes and before 3 pm.
A warm shower an hour before bed helps your body cool down for sleep.
Write tomorrow's worries on paper before bed to clear your head.
Aim for 7–9 hours; track for a week to see your real average.
Get morning sunlight within an hour of waking; it sets your body clock.
Avoid heavy, spicy meals late at night.
Limit alcohol; it fragments sleep even if it helps you fall asleep.
Use the bed only for sleep, not for laptop work.
Try 4-7-8 breathing in bed: in for 4, hold 7, out for 8.
Snoring loudly or waking unrefreshed? Mention it to a doctor; sleep apnoea is common.

eat.eat: Dal, rajma or chana with every lunch
eat.why: Pulses give protein and fibre that keep you full longer.
Healthy fats and protein without excess salt.
Probiotics support digestion; soft drinks add empty sugar.
Whole fruit keeps the fibre; juice is mostly sugar.

eat.eat: Millets (ragi, jowar, bajra) a few times a week
eat.why: More fibre and minerals, slower energy release.
Easy way to cut calories and boost nutrients.

eat.eat: Eggs, paneer, tofu or fish for protein
eat.why: Lean protein supports muscle; processed meats are high in salt and preservatives.
You control the oil, salt and portion.

eat.eat: Water through the day (about 2–3 litres, more in heat)
eat.why: Mild dehydration hurts focus and energy.

eat.eat: Sprouts or chana chaat as a snack
eat.why: Protein and fibre instead of sugar and refined flour.
Iron, folate and vitamins; light cooking preserves them.
Satisfies a craving with less sugar.
Better digestion and sleep.
Flavour with less sodium.

eat.eat: Oats, poha or idli for breakfast
eat.why: Steady energy through the morning.
Natural electrolytes without added sugar.

eat.eat: Mindful portions at buffets and parties
eat.why: Use a smaller plate and fill it once.
Repeatedly heated oil forms harmful compounds.
Good for gut health.

eat.eat: A balanced thali: grain, dal, veg, curd, salad
eat.why: Covers most nutrients in one plate.

posture: Sitting: feet flat, knees at hip height, lower back supported, screen top at eye level.
Standing: weight even on both feet, knees soft, shoulders relaxed down and back.
Walking: look ahead not at your phone, swing your arms, land mid-foot.
Running: short quick steps, land under your hips, relaxed shoulders, start slow.
Lifting: bend your knees, keep the load close, don't twist while lifting.
Phone: raise it to eye level instead of bending your neck down.
Laptop: use a stand plus external keyboard and mouse for long sessions.
Every 30 minutes of sitting, stand and move for 2–3 minutes.
Sleeping: on your side with a pillow between your knees, or on your back with one under them.
Driving: seat upright, hips back, mirrors set so you don't slouch.
Carrying bags: use a backpack with both straps rather than one shoulder.
Typing: wrists straight and elbows at about 90 degrees.
Standing desk: alternate sitting and standing every 30–45 minutes.
Picking up kids: squat down and lift with your legs, not your back.
Check yourself: if your ear is in front of your shoulder, tuck your chin back.
